Srila Prabhupada writes in purport to Srimad Bhagavatam 3.1.32: “The pure devotee of the Lord is always in company with the Lord by thinking of Him. Yet, in the particular context of time and place, the transcendental emotions take a different turn, and this breaks the mental equilibrium of the devotee. Lord Caitanya displayed the typical example of transcendental ecstasy, as we can understand from the life of this incarnation of God.” Discuss this statement with reference to examples from Srimad Bhagavatam Cantos 1 & 2, and optionally, the lives of vaisnava acaryas.
Briefly describe how Arjuna got the Pasupati weapon from Lord Siva. (38)

Srila Prabhupada writes in purport to Srimad Bhagavatam 3.1.14: “But Duryodhana was so foolish that he dared to insult Vidura. This was due to his bad association with Sakuni, his maternal uncle, as well as with his friend Karṇa, who always encouraged Duryodhana in his nefarious acts.” Discuss the significance of this statement in relation to your personal practice of Krsna consciousness. Give reference to Srimad Bhagavatam 3.1.14, verse and purport, and relevant reference to the bhakti sastras in your response.

Explain Vidura’s attitude to the insulting words of Duryodhana. Discuss the significance of this example in in relation to your practice of Krsna consciousness. Give reference to Srimad Bhagavatam 3.1.16, verse and purport, and this section in general, and relevant reference to the bhakti sastras in your response.

Srila Prabhupada writes in the purport to Srimad Bhagavatam 3.1.17, “In the land of Bharatavarsa there are many hundreds and thousands of places of pilgrimage distributed all over the country, and by traditional practice the common man visits such holy places during all seasons of the year.” Discuss the significance of this statement with reference to the example of Vidura. Give reference to 3.1.17, verse and purport, in your response.

“There are still many devotees of the Lord lingering there in ecstasy in search of Krsna and His childhood associates, the gopis.” Discuss how this statement reflects Srila Prabhupa’s mood, with reference to Srimad Bhagavatam 3.1.24, verse & purport.
